goal: Speeds up wallet descriptor loading by caching a hash of the canonical descriptor string instead of recomputing it on every comparison, fixing a performance regression from a prior PR.
Also tidies up several review comments and descriptor-string edge cases left over from that earlier work.

Sjors raised nonblocking design questions about where the cache should live, resolved amicably (Sjors, achow101).

result.summary: This PR caches a hash of the canonical descriptor string on WalletDescriptor construction so that HasWalletDescriptor and UpdateFrom no longer recompute the canonical string on every comparison, fixing a performance regression introduced by a prior descriptor PR (#35445). It also cleans up several review comments from that PR: clarifying apostrophe-handling logic in descriptor string generation, documenting UpdateFrom, removing the WalletDescriptor default constructor, and adjusting the backwards-compatibility test matrix to add a 31.1 node.
result.problem: Wallet descriptor comparisons (used when loading descriptor wallets, especially with miniscript) were recomputing an expensive canonical string on every call, causing a measured slowdown; users and testers loading wallets with many or complex descriptors felt this as slow wallet loads.

open_concerns: CI is failing: maflcko notes the 31.0/31.1 swap in wallet_backwards_compatibility.py broke the test because get_previous_releases.py no longer has the file the test expects; polespinasa suggests adding 31.1 instead of replacing 31.0.
Minor nits (naming of Equals/IsCanonicallyEquivalent, whitespace, ternary style) raised by davidgumberg and Sjors, mostly addressed but some very recent.
resolved_concerns: Sjors's request to document that comparison is only over the canonical string: addressed by renaming to IsCanonicallyEquivalent with added docs.
polespinasa's concern about default-constructed WalletDescriptor never initializing the hash: addressed by removing the default constructor entirely.
davidgumberg's suggestion to lazily compute and cache the hash rather than assert it's set: implemented via GetCanonicalHash().
polespinasa's suggestion to deduplicate the apostrophe-handling switch statement: implemented via DetermineApostropheUse helper.

The regression originates in an already-shipped release path (label 'Needs Backport (32.x)'), so unresolved it continues to slow down wallet loads for descriptor wallet users, particularly those with miniscript descriptors, until backported. It is not a fund-safety or correctness issue, so it sits at P2 rather than P1.

result.card: This PR is a follow-up to #35445 that fixes a performance regression in wallet descriptor comparison: WalletDescriptor now caches a hash of its canonical descriptor string instead of recomputing it on every HasWalletDescriptor/UpdateFrom call. hebasto and rkrux both measured roughly a 50% reduction in wallet_miniscript.py test time confirming the fix works, and polespinasa gave concept ACK after several review rounds the author addressed (renaming, documentation, removing an unsafe default constructor). It carries a 'Needs Backport (32.x)' label, indicating the underlying regression already shipped. However, CI is currently failing because the 31.0-to-31.1 swap in the backwards-compatibility test broke get_previous_releases.py lookups, per maflcko's latest comment, so the head commit needs another fix before review is safe from being invalidated. No blocking objections to the approach exist; remaining comments are nits.
